title: What each pharmacist records, and for how long, on a federal controlled-substance prescription transfer
rule_summary: On a refill-purpose transfer of Schedule III-V prescription information, 21 CFR 1306.25(b) requires the transfer to be communicated directly between two licensed pharmacists. The transferring pharmacist must write 'VOID' on the face of the invalidated prescription (for an electronic prescription, information that it has been transferred must be added to the prescription record); record on the reverse of the invalidated prescription, or for an electronic prescription in the prescription record, the name, address and DEA registration number of the pharmacy to which it was transferred and the name of the pharmacist receiving the information; and record the date of the transfer and the name of the pharmacist transferring the information. For a paper prescription, or one received orally and reduced to writing, the receiving pharmacist must write 'transfer' on the face of the transferred prescription, reduce to writing all information 21 CFR 1306.05 requires on a prescription, and include the date of issuance of the original prescription, the original number of refills authorized, the date of original dispensing, the number of valid refills remaining and the date(s) and locations of previous refill(s), the name, address, DEA registration number and prescription number of the pharmacy from which the information was transferred, the name of the pharmacist who transferred it, and the name, address, DEA registration number and prescription number of the pharmacy from which the prescription was originally filled. For an electronic prescription transferred electronically, the transferring pharmacist provides, with the original electronic prescription data, the date of the original dispensing, the number of refills remaining and the date(s) and locations of previous refills, the transferring pharmacy's name, address, DEA registration number and prescription number for each dispensing, the name of the transferring pharmacist, and the name, address, DEA registration number and prescription number of the pharmacy that originally filled the prescription, if different; the receiving pharmacist creates an electronic record for the prescription that includes the receiving pharmacist's name and all of the transferred information. Under 1306.25(c) the original and transferred prescriptions must be maintained for two years from the date of last refill, and under 1306.25(d) pharmacies electronically accessing the same prescription record must satisfy all information requirements of a manual mode for prescription transferal. On the transfer of an electronic Schedule II-V prescription for initial dispensing, 21 CFR 1306.08(f) requires the prescription to move from one retail pharmacy to another in its electronic form, with no intermediary converting it to another form such as facsimile and no alteration of its required contents, communicated directly between two licensed pharmacists. The transferring pharmacist adds to the electronic prescription record information that the prescription has been transferred, the name, address and DEA registration number of the pharmacy to which it was transferred and the name of the pharmacist receiving it, and the date of the transfer and the name of the transferring pharmacist; the receiving pharmacist adds the word 'transfer' to the electronic prescription record, annotates it with the name, address and DEA registration number of the pharmacy from which it was transferred and the name of the pharmacist who transferred it, and records the date of the transfer and the name of the pharmacist receiving it. Prescription processing software may capture this information and populate the fields, but the transferring or receiving pharmacist must ensure the populated information is complete and accurate. Under 1306.08(h) the electronic records documenting the transfer must be maintained for two years from the date of the transfer by both the transferring and the receiving pharmacy.
exam_relevance: Tests what the transferring and receiving pharmacists record on each federal transfer pathway, and which retention clock applies: two years from the date of last refill on a refill-purpose transfer, and two years from the date of transfer, at both pharmacies, on an initial-dispensing electronic transfer.

authority.name: Transfer between pharmacies of prescription information for Schedules III, IV, and V controlled substances for refill purposes
Transfer of an electronic controlled-substance prescription for initial dispensing

numeric_facts.fact: Retention of the original and transferred prescriptions after a refill-purpose transfer
numeric_facts.conditions: From the date of last refill (21 CFR 1306.25(c))

numeric_facts.fact: Retention of the electronic records documenting an initial-dispensing transfer
numeric_facts.conditions: From the date of the transfer, by both the transferring and the receiving pharmacy (21 CFR 1306.08(h))

exceptions: Pharmacies electronically accessing the same prescription record must still satisfy all information requirements of a manual mode for prescription transferal (21 CFR 1306.25(d)).
common_confusions: Counting the refill-transfer retention period from the date of the transfer rather than from the date of last refill.
Assuming only the transferring pharmacy keeps the record of an initial-dispensing electronic transfer, when 21 CFR 1306.08(h) requires both pharmacies to keep it.
Treating automatically populated transfer fields as relieving the pharmacist of checking that they are complete and accurate.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1306.25(b)-(d) and 1306.08(f) and (h) read on 2026-09-11 in the current eCFR section pages (shown as up to date as of 9/09/2026) and in the eCFR versioner text of 21 CFR part 1306 as of 2026-09-08. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
